# Document replacement process

This example process shows one successful update and an explicit conflict exit.
Read the overview first, then follow the input, processing, and completion slides.
Let $r$ be the stored revision.

$$
r_{next} = r + 1
$$

Send the full document with the revision that you read.

```typescript
const update = {
  documentId: "4e7efb70-6686-4f94-aa51-f97d40abb677",
  expectedRevision: 3,
  document: completeDocument,
};
```

slides.title: Complete process
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Start["Start"] --> Read["Read current document"]
  Read --> Edit["Prepare complete replacement"]
  Edit --> Validate["Validate document"]
  Validate --> Compare{"Revision matches?"}
  Compare -->|Yes| Commit["Commit replacement"]
  Compare -->|No| Conflict["Conflict: read again"]
  Conflict --> Read
  Commit --> Result["Return saved revision"]
  Result --> End["End"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
This deck explains how a complete replacement is saved without overwriting a newer revision.
The overview connects reading, editing, validation, revision checking, and commit through to Return saved revision.
A conflict returns to Read current document instead of overwriting a newer update.
The next slides isolate the input, processing, and completion stages of this same path.

slides.title: Input and start
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Start["Start"] --> Read["Read current document"]
  Read --> Edit["Prepare complete replacement"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
The overview begins with Read current document; this slide isolates that input stage.
The current document and its revision are the inputs to Prepare complete replacement.
Keep stable block and slide IDs where the content has the same role.
The prepared document and the revision that was read pass to Validate document on the next slide.
Validation and persistence are omitted here.

slides.title: Core processing
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Edit["Prepare complete replacement"] --> Validate["Validate document"]
  Validate --> Compare{"Revision matches?"}
  Compare -->|Yes| Commit["Commit replacement"]
  Compare -->|No| Conflict["Conflict: read again"]
  Conflict --> Read["Read current document"]

slides.title: Output and end
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Commit["Commit replacement"] --> Result["Return saved revision"]
  Result --> End["End"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Commit replacement continues from the preceding processing slide.
Return saved revision confirms persistence and completes the replacement process.
A saved document is not proof that Mermaid or LaTeX rendered correctly.
Open the viewer for a browser check, or report that rendering is unverified.
The next revision is $r_{next} = r + 1$.

blocks.markdown:
## Failure boundary

A validation error does not commit a replacement.
A revision conflict requires a new read, not a blind retry.
The independent deck below keeps the conflict decision visible while the main deck changes slides.

slides.title: Conflict recovery
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Conflict["Conflict: read again"] --> Read["Read current document"]
  Read --> Edit["Prepare complete replacement"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Rebuild the replacement from the new stored document and use its revision.
Do not discard another writer's change without an explicit decision.
